data.readme: This document explains what each field of the resume payload means, which parts are ready to paste into a finished resume as-is, and which are background material only. Read this before reading the resume itself. Nothing here restates resume content — where a rule needs to name a piece of the payload it carries a path instead, e.g. resume.jobs[].highlights[].summary.

disclosure.rationale: These fields exist for tailoring and outreach, not for a public feed. The public projection redacts them structurally, but a document generated from this data should never include them either.
rules: Never print an email address or phone number in a generated document unless the user explicitly asks for one to be included.

An entry with `publish: false` is withheld from the public website feed only. It is not a signal to omit that entry from a tailored resume or cover letter — treat every entry in this document as eligible material regardless of its `publish` value.

joins.name: highlight-to-lead-selection
joins.description: A role family names highlights to lead with by id; join on that id to find the actual highlight content.
joins.on_unmatched_left: A highlight with no role family referencing it is still eligible — role families are a starting point, not a filter.
joins.on_unmatched_right: An id in lead_highlight_ids with no matching highlight is a data error — stop and say so rather than guessing which highlight was meant.
joins.failure_mode: Matching on summary text instead of id silently pairs the wrong highlight after any wording edit.

sections.title: Professional summary
sections.description: A short paragraph introducing the candidate.
sections.purpose: The one part of the document every reader finishes; sets the frame for everything after it.

rules: Keep to three sentences or fewer.
fields.example: Backend engineer with six years building API services.

sections.title: Highlights
sections.purpose: The evidence a tailored resume selects from.
sections.ordering: Most relevant to the target posting first, not chronological.
selection: Prefer highlights whose tech list overlaps the posting's stack.

fields.example: Cut route-recalculation latency by adding a bounded cache.

fields.description: First-person material for a cover letter only.
rules: Never appears on a resume, only in a cover letter, and only when it fits the posting.

fields.description: Withholds this one highlight from the public website feed only. The same flag, with the same meaning, exists at every withholdable level of the resume — jobs, skill groups, skills, certifications, education, personal projects, locations and links. It has no bearing on a tailored resume or cover letter: an entry withheld from a published website is often exactly the one to lead with in an application.
rules: Never treat `publish: false` as an instruction to omit the entry from a tailored resume or cover letter — it governs the public website feed only, not what Claude may draw on.

terms.meaning: Mix of on-site and remote days.

rules: Never state a figure without its basis available to cite if asked.
Round to the precision the basis actually supports; do not add false precision.

role_families.note: Lead with the payments idempotency work for anything mentioning reliability or on-call ownership.

cautions: The two employers in this example are fictional; do not treat their names as real companies when reasoning about the data.
fine_tuning_data.logistics is background for judgement only — never print a salary expectation unless the user asks for one to be included.
